Article title: Little Rose

Article text:
Roisin, 40-plus woman, walks around a body lying on the ground, covered in a shroud. She lifts it, looks, puts it down. Starts walking again. Stops, as if something occurred to her, goes back, lifts, and looks again.
Kate, also a 40-plus woman, walks onto the stage holding a manilla folder.
Kate: Sorry? Are those my only options?
Roisin: You can be neither. Both would probably be too much work.
Roisin: Roisin. Means “little rose.” I assume that “little” is supposed to be cute. But it makes me think of those cheap spray roses that fill out bouquets. If you give someone a dozen of those, they won’t think cute, they'll just think you're cheap.

Title: Show HN: Vondet – A planning board Claude keeps, so you don't have to
Article title: Vondet — Claude keeps your plan on a board, so you don't have to.
Description: A board your AI writes to. Instead of a fresh summary every conversation, it stacks into one plan.
HN text: Hi HN, Vondet is a planning board, but you don't write on it.
Claude writes to Vondet via an MCP connection. As I worked on my product with Claude, my Markdown files gradually piled up. There were files like “beta plan”, “v1 plan”, and “development plan v0.5.”
I asked Claude to tidy them up. It created a new file “next-milestone plan v0.1” Haha. I spent too much time trying to remember what I planned. So I built a tool to keep plans and decisions in one place. It's ready for Claude to refer to in future sessions. Claude can use the board to:
- Read: Tasks, decision logs, topics
- Plan: Capture, update, and order t…
